hostess.note: Also a woman who has guests at her home: "Thank the hostess for dinner."
ex: The hostess showed us to a table by the window.
Ask the hostess if there is a free table.
The hostess at the door said the wait is twenty minutes.
She works as a hostess in a busy restaurant.

porno.note: Informal; the neutral word is "porn" or "pornography."

salsa.note: In the US, "salsa" is very often a spicy tomato sauce; it is also a dance.

joint.note: Most often "joint" means shared ("a joint account") or a body part like the knee.

optimism.note: Uncountable: a lot of optimism (not "an optimism").
ex: Her optimism helped the team stay strong.
There is new optimism about the economy this year.
I like your optimism, but we need a plan.
His optimism makes him a great person to work with.

mademoiselle.note: A French title for a young woman; in English it is used mostly about France.
ex: "Thank you, mademoiselle," said the waiter with a smile.
In Paris, the shop assistant called her mademoiselle.
The hotel staff greeted her with "Bonjour, mademoiselle."
In the novel, the young mademoiselle lives in Paris.

khan.note: Most often "Khan" is a family name; as a title for a ruler it is historical.
ex: The khan ruled a huge empire on the steppe.
Each tribe was led by its own khan.
The khan's army crossed the river in winter.
In the museum, we saw the khan's golden throne.

pickup.note: Also called a "pickup truck." It can also mean collecting: "The pickup time is 5 p.m."
ex: He drives an old pickup to work every day.
Put the boxes in the back of the pickup.
My dad bought a new pickup last month.
A pickup is great for work on a farm.
In the past, important news came by telegraph.
The telegraph changed the way people communicated.
He sent a message to his family by telegraph.
Telegraph lines ran along the railroad tracks.

junior.note: Most often "junior" means younger or lower in rank: "a junior manager."
ex: Our company is hiring two juniors for the web team.
As a junior, she learns a lot from senior developers.
The junior asked the team lead to check his code.
He worked as a junior for a year before his promotion.

sort.note: Most often "sort" means kind: "What sort of music do you like?" For plants, "variety" is usual.
ex: What sort of apples do you grow in your garden?
This sort of tomato grows well in a cold climate.
The shop sells three sorts of coffee beans.
Which sort of grape is best for making wine?

funk.note: Uncountable. "In a funk" means in a sad mood.

mainstream.note: Most often used before a noun: "mainstream music," "mainstream media."
ex: Her music slowly became part of the mainstream.
These ideas are now part of the mainstream.
The band was too strange for the mainstream.
Electric cars are quickly moving into the mainstream.

paranoia.note: Uncountable: a lot of paranoia (not "a paranoia").

idol.note: Most often "idol" means a famous person many people love: "He was my childhood idol."

socialist.note: Most often used as an adjective: "a socialist party," "socialist ideas."

homage.note: Common phrase: "pay homage to" someone or something.
ex: The movie is an homage to old westerns.
Her new album is an homage to eighties pop music.
His painting pays homage to the great masters.
The restaurant's menu is an homage to his grandmother's cooking.

glamour.note: Uncountable. Also spelled "glamor" in the US, but "glamour" is more common.
ex: Many young people dream of the glamour of Hollywood.
The party had an air of glamour and style.
She loves the glamour of big fashion shows.
The job has little glamour, but the pay is good.
A cactus needs very little water to grow.
I have a small cactus on my desk at work.
Don't touch the cactus because it has sharp spines.
The desert is full of tall cacti.

SI.note: SI has several uses; in science it is the metric system of units: "SI units."
ex: The meter is the SI unit of length.
Please use SI units in your lab report.
SI stands for the International System of Units.
The kilogram is one of the SI base units.
Regular exercise speeds up your metabolism.
My metabolism slowed down after I turned forty.
Some people have a fast metabolism and stay thin.
Poor sleep can slow down your metabolism.

jumper.note: British for a sweater; in the US a "jumper" is a dress, and "sweater" is the usual word.

highlight.note: Often a verb: "Highlight the key words." As a noun, it is the best part of something.

true.note: Most often "true" means correct, not false: "Is it true?" "That is not true."
ex: He is a true fan and never misses a game.
She found her true love in college.
A true friend helps you when things are hard.
This small restaurant serves true Italian pizza.

patch.note: Most often "patch" is a small area or piece: "a patch of grass," "a patch on a jacket."

ex: The water made a vortex as it went down the drain.
A tornado is a powerful vortex of spinning air.
The small boat was pulled into a vortex in the river.
Scientists study how a vortex forms behind airplane wings.
The squire owned most of the land around the village.
The old squire lived in a large house on the hill.
Everyone in the village knew and respected the squire.
In the novel, the squire invites the doctor to dinner.
Every device on a network has an IP address.
The website blocked my IP after too many logins.
Can you check your IP address for me?
The company traced the attack to a foreign IP.

pack.note: Most often "pack" is a verb: "Pack your bag." As a noun: "a pack of gum."
